chunks: The Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله ascended the pulpit one day, then praised Allah, extolled Him, and sent blessings upon His Prophets عليهم السلام. Then he said:

"O people, let those of you who are present convey it to those who are absent: whoever grants respite to an insolvent debtor shall have with Allah, Mighty and Majestic, every day the reward of charity equal to the amount of his wealth until he fully recovers it."
And Abu Abdillah عليه السلام said:
"Allah, Mighty and Majestic, said: ‘And if someone is in hardship, then postponement until ease; and that you give in charity is better for you, if you only knew.’"
If he is insolvent, then give charity to him from your wealth, for that is better for you.

key_terms.تَصَدَّقُوا: to give as charity, here by remitting the debt
key_terms.فَنَظِرَةٌ: a postponement or delay in repayment
key_terms.مَيْسَرَةٍ: a state of ease or financial ability
key_terms.مُعْسِرًا: an insolvent person who is unable to repay a debt

ai.seo_question: What is the reward for giving respite to an insolvent debtor in Islam?
ai.summary: This hadith teaches the virtue of showing mercy to an insolvent debtor by granting him time to repay. It also cites the Qur'anic command to defer repayment for one in hardship and states that remitting the debt as charity is even better. The narration highlights both the legal and moral excellence of financial leniency.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications: Hadith.1701 - The Messenger of Allah (swt) (peace be upon him and his family) once ascended the pulpit, praised Allah (swt), glorified Him, and sent blessings upon His Prophets (as). Then he said: "O people, let those who are present convey this to those who are absent: Whoever grants respite to an insolvent debtor shall receive from Allah (swt), the Almighty, the reward of charity equal to the amount of his debt every day until he collects it."

Abu Abdullah (as) said: "Allah (swt), the Almighty, said:
‘And if someone is in hardship, then [let there be] postponement until [a time of] ease. But if you give [as charity], it is better for you, if you only knew' (Surah Al-Baqarah 2:280).
[This means] if you know that he is insolvent, then forgive him his debt; that is better for you.”
